q: You manage containers with `count = length(var.sites)` where `sites = ["blog", "shop", "docs"]`. You remove `"shop"`. What does the plan do?
options: Replaces the container at index 1 (shop becomes docs) and destroys index 2
explain: `count` tracks instances by position. Removing an element shifts later elements down, so `[1]` now gets docs' config (forcing replacement) and `[2]` disappears. `for_each` with keys avoids this.

q: Which value can be passed directly to `for_each`?
explain: `for_each` accepts a map or a set of strings. Convert lists with `toset()`, and turn lists of objects into a map with a `for` expression: `{ for o in var.list : o.name => o }`. A number is for `count`.

q: Plan fails with `Invalid for_each argument ... values derived from resource attributes that cannot be determined until apply`. What's the fix?
options: Run `terraform apply -target` on the dependency first, every time
Build the `for_each` keys from values known at plan time (variables, locals, static names) and put computed values in the map's values instead
Switch to `count = length(...)` of the same computed list
explain: Keys must be known at plan time because they become resource addresses. Computed values (IDs, random names) can be used as values but not as keys. `-target` is a one-off workaround; `count` has the same limitation.

q: What does `{ for name, s in var.services : s.image => name... }` produce?
options: A map from image to a list of service names using it
An error because of duplicate keys
A map from service name to image
explain: The `...` after the value enables grouping mode: values for the same key are collected into a list. Without `...`, duplicate keys would be an error.

q: `docker_container.web` uses `for_each`. Which expression gives a list of all their names?
explain: A `for_each` resource is a map of instances, and splat `[*]` only works on lists. Use a `for` expression or `values(docker_container.web)[*].name`.

q: You set `create_before_destroy = true` on `docker_container.api` with a fixed `name = "shipit-api"`. Changing the image fails. Why?
options: The image must be destroyed first
The new container can't be created while the old one still holds the unique name
explain: create_before_destroy creates the replacement first. Any resource with a unique, unchanging name (containers, S3 buckets, security group names) conflicts. Use varying names (`name_prefix`, a suffix) or drop the setting.

q: A container bind-mounts a config file generated by `local_file`. When the file content changes, the container should restart. Which is the cleanest solution?
explain: `replace_triggered_by` replaces the resource when the referenced resource changes, even if the container's own arguments (the same file path) didn't change. `depends_on` only orders operations.

q: Which statements about `check` blocks are true? (select all)
options: A failed assertion produces a warning and the run continues
They can contain a scoped data source, such as an `http` health check
They're evaluated on plan and apply
explain: Checks are non-blocking: they warn. They can declare data sources scoped to the check and run on every plan/apply (and on a schedule in HCP Terraform). Use pre/postconditions when a failure must stop the run.

q: Which `lifecycle` setting is appropriate when an autoscaler legitimately changes a resource's desired count outside Terraform?
explain: `ignore_changes` stops Terraform from reverting attributes that something else manages. Add a comment saying who owns the attribute, and don't use it to hide drift you don't understand.

q: What does `try(var.config.tls.port, 443)` return when `var.config` has no `tls` attribute?
explain: `try` returns the first argument that evaluates without an error. Accessing a missing attribute errors, so the fallback `443` is returned.

q: You need an ACM certificate in `us-east-1` while everything else is in `eu-central-1`. How?
options: Add `provider "aws" { alias = "us_east_1"  region = "us-east-1" }` and set `provider = aws.us_east_1` on the resource
Run Terraform twice with different `AWS_REGION` values
Use a `dynamic` block for the region
explain: Provider aliases give you additional configurations of the same provider; the `provider` meta-argument selects one per resource. (Recent AWS provider versions also accept a per-resource `region` argument, but aliases are the general mechanism across all providers.)

options: A migration container connects to Postgres by a hard-coded hostname string, so there's no reference to the Postgres resource
An IAM policy must be attached before an app that uses it starts, but the app resource doesn't reference the attachment
Every resource in a module, to be safe
explain: `depends_on` is for dependencies Terraform can't infer from references. An existing reference already creates the edge, and blanket `depends_on` makes values unknown longer and plans noisier.

q: What's the difference between a `precondition` and a `postcondition` on a resource?
options: Preconditions are warnings; postconditions are errors
Preconditions check assumptions before the resource is planned/applied; postconditions check guarantees about the result and can reference `self`
explain: Both fail the run. Preconditions validate inputs and assumptions up front; postconditions validate the resulting object's attributes via `self`.

q: You want to replace a container whenever `var.app_version` changes, but the container's arguments don't use that variable. What works?
options: A `terraform_data` resource with `input = var.app_version`, referenced in `replace_triggered_by`
explain: `replace_triggered_by` only accepts managed resources or their attributes. `terraform_data` turns a variable into a resource that is replaced whenever its input changes, which then triggers the container.
